notes.text: The twelve Australian Museum specimens are individually identified in Table 3. No institution-scoped identifier or matching Australian Museum matā was found in the existing MoSA collection. The source reports study-time holdings, not verified current custody. Extraction covers identification and material, Table 1 acquisition rows with consistent identifiers, Table 2 metrics and form except its disputed E70735 row, and Appendix Part 2 use interpretations with their confidence. Table headings are retained with their cells, separated by semicolons; only layout whitespace and typographic ligatures are normalised. Acquisition dates are not making dates, and the Robins donor statement concerns some items in the collection, not a proven 1860 history for each specimen. Table 1 prints E65164, whereas Tables 2–3, Figure 2 and the appendix use E65154; the Bard acquisition and quoted cave findspot are withheld pending confirmation. Table 2 prints E70735, whereas Table 1’s range, Table 3, Figure 1b and the appendix use E30735; no E70735 alias, thirteenth object or metric claims from that row are asserted. Figure 7’s caption identifies panel b as A18927 and panel c as A18928, but the photographed labels read A18928 on b and A18927 on c, consistent with Table 2’s respective rectangular and triangular blade shapes. No figure-to-object image links are asserted from the reversed caption. Source-specific identity follows the consistent specimen entries without claiming that either discrepancy has been resolved. Table 3 and Appendix Part 2 differ slightly in the proposed contact material for E30737 and E30739; both wordings are retained separately. Appendix Part 1 microscopic observations, remaining Part 2 surface/residue fields, and extended functional or authenticity arguments are outside this selective extraction. Proposed contact materials and wooden handles are interpretations, not the objects’ constituent materials. In particular E30736’s use and contact material remain uncertain. The original is a user-supplied Project MUSE PDF, inspected for this extraction; the issue is dated 2018 and its article copyright is © 2019 University of Hawai‘i Press. No redistribution or figure-reuse licence appears in the supplied file. It remains in ignored local storage, with its download watermark private; no capture or image is registered. Figures 1–7 and the acknowledgments were reviewed: drawings and micrographs are evidence but not cleared publishable assets.
